vocab.definition: the ratio of reactants and products in an equation.
the reactant that runs out first and stops the reaction.
a reactant that is not all used up.
the ratio of moles from the balanced equation.

misconceptions.wrong: The reactant with the bigger mass is in excess.
misconceptions.right: Compare MOLES, not masses, to find excess.
Convert to moles first using the molar mass.
Often one is in excess and is left over.

infoPanels.title: WORKED EXAMPLE
workedSteps: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Find MgO from 48 g Mg.

questions.text: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. Calculate the mass of water from 4 g of H₂. (Mᵣ H₂=2, H₂O=18) [3 marks]
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Calculate the mass of CaCO₃ needed to make 5.6 g CaO. (CaCO₃=100, CaO=56) [3 marks]
Explain what is meant by the limiting reactant. [1 mark]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: Convert masses to ______ first. The reactant that runs out is the ______ reactant.

questions.text: Explain how you would decide which reactant is in excess. [2 marks]
If 24 g of Mg makes 40 g MgO, calculate the MgO from 12 g of Mg. [2 marks]

footer.tip: Always convert to moles, use the balanced ratio, then convert back to mass.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does using excess of one reactant ensure the other is fully used up?
